text.p: Westpac Banking Corp Ltd's said on Tuesday its efficiency ratio, which measures expenses to income, worsened to 63.6 percent in the six months to September 30 from 61.5 percent in the first half and 60.6 percent in the 1994/95 year.
A Westpac spokesman said this was largely due to extra costs incurred in acquiring two new banks, Western Australian-based Challenge Bank and Trust Bank of New Zealand.
The spokesman told Reuters that this efficiency ratio was expected to improve in the current year to September 30, 1997 as the two banks are integrated and rationalised.
Westpac said the expense ratio adjusted for the Challenge and Trust Bank acquisitions fell to 63.3 percent in 1995/96 from 65.6 percent in 1994/95.
Non-interest expenses as a proportion of average assets also rose to 2.78 percent in the second half from 2.49 percent in the first half and 2.74 percent in 1994/95.
Earlier Westpac reported that net profit before abnormals rose 11.5 percent to A$1.132 billion from A$1.015 billion the previous year.
Analysts had on average expected a net profit before abnormals of A$1.12 billion.
However the profit of A$1.132 billion included A$121 million of bad debt charges, down sharply from A$330 million in 1994/95.
